gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.
A bank manager is a person; 'management' is the activity and 'manage' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: She apologized for the ___ caused by the delay (CONVENIENT).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — the delay was a bad thing
gaps.explanation: A delay causes inconvenience (negative prefix in- + noun); the sentence needs the noun, not the adjectives.
The noun of 'wise' is 'wisdom' (-dom suffix); 'wisedom' is a common misspelling.

gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.
The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.
The suffix -en forms verbs from adjectives: thicken. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ until Thursday (SCHEDULE).
gaps.hint: arranged for a new time (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again/afresh: rescheduled means given a new time. The passive needs the past participle.
